quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Information security analysts plan, implement, upgrade or monitor security measures that protect computer networks and information, assess systems for security risks, and may respond to security breaches and viruses.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Information Security Analysts) include Security Analyst, Information Security Specialist, Information Security Officer and Network Security Analyst.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What an information security analyst does
paragraphs: Information security analysts plan, implement, upgrade or monitor security measures that protect computer networks and information, assess systems for security risks, and may respond to security breaches and viruses.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Information Security Analysts. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Develop plans that safeguard computer files against accidental or unauthorised modification or destruction.
Carry out risk assessments and test data processing systems.
Encrypt data transmissions and set up firewalls to protect confidential information.
Review violations of security procedures and discuss them with the people involved.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.
In India, the UGC specification of degrees lists B.Tech and B.E. as four-year bachelor's degrees entered after 10+2.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering; BCA (Bachelor of Computer Applications); Systems Administrator.
Less common routes on the map: MCA (Master of Computer Applications).
